title: Logical Uncertainty and Calibration: Do LLMs Have Well-Calibrated Logical Beliefs?

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Logical uncertainty is a key open problem for Vingean reflection and safe self-referential reasoning. If LLMs are systematically miscalibrated on logical tasks, this directly informs the viability of formal agent foundations proposals that assume logical uncertainty.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Presenting logic problems to an LLM and collecting confidence scores is purely inference-based, requiring no training. Measuring ECE is a standard metric. Logic problems of varying difficulty can be generated or sourced from benchmarks. Minimal compute requirements.

narrow_scope.reasoning: 200 logic problems, ask for answer + confidence, compute ECE by complexity level. Single clear deliverable (calibration plot by logical complexity). Easily achievable in 30 hours with time to spare.
